findings.description: Removing the numbered narration comments from TRANSFORMS left entry 2 (stripping the AGENT_INIT_VERSION env block, lines ~84-86) with no explanatory comment at its call site at all — entries 1 and 5 are still covered by the new TEMPLATE_HEADER_SHA JSDoc and a retained comment respectively, but entry 2's old `// 2. No published version to pin: the tooling is built, not installed.` is gone, so that rationale now lives only implicitly in the HEADER text, one level removed from the actual regex/replacement pair. Entries 4 and 6 also lost their one-liners but are largely self-evident from the substituted content. Net effect is a minor, patchy readability dip, not a structural problem — worth a one-line comment restore on entry 2 if the file is touched again.

refuted_findings.description: Claimed the delta removed id-token: write from the rendered .github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml but left it in the template it renders from, breaking the template/rendered-file sync test and shipping an unused permission to downstream scaffold users.
refuted_findings.refutation: git show HEAD:templates/github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml (HEAD = 55fa2ac62e3441788aa673801ff84656f768d99d, confirmed equal to the PR's actual headRefOid) contains no id-token line; git diff 6b2e1d897c1892e5d5a4b405ced3fd133f5bd505..HEAD -- templates/github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml shows the commit explicitly removing it (`-      id-token: write`). The reviewer read the live working-tree copy of this file, which was left in a stale, uncommitted, reverted state (re-adding id-token: write and undoing two other parts of the delta) before the review began — most likely the CI action's own config-restore mechanism, or session state, rather than the PR's real committed content. A dedicated review-validator (opus) independently reproduced this via git grep against both SHAs and reached the same conclusion.

process_issues.description: The working tree showed templates/github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml as modified (stale, reverted to the pre-delta state) before the review started, visible in the initial git status. I did not proactively flag this specific file as restore-affected in the security reviewer's brief, only giving a general instruction to use git diff/git show. The security reviewer partly read the live working-tree file instead and raised a false-positive important finding as a result (caught by validation). Future incremental runs touching this path should explicitly instruct reviewers to use `git show <sha>:<path>` rather than Read/cat for any file under templates/ or the other config-restore paths, per SKILL.md section 2.
